title: Tiered commitment credits + dynamic batch multiplier for embeddings pricing pilot
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Validate a two-dimensional pricing incentive for embeddings customers: (1) up-front committed credits that materialize as per-vector discounts, and (2) an automated 'dynamic batch multiplier' that increases effective discounting as observed batch sizes grow in a billing period. We expect this combination to (a) improve revenue predictability via commitments, (b) lower marginal cost for heavy batch rerank/embedding workloads, and (c) reduce churn for customers sensitive to per-vector unit price variability.

Hypothesis: Customers who commit to a 3–12 month credit contract will (i) increase monthly usage by >=10% QoQ and (ii) shift a higher percentage of calls into batched flows when a batch-multiplier discount applies, improving unit economics for Redwood without degrading latency-critical single-call use-cases.

Experiment design: Two-arm randomized pilot for eligible customers (self-serve and sales-assisted):
- Arm A (Commitment + Batch Multiplier): Offer 3-tier commitment credit sizes (S/M/L) with associated baseline per-vector discount (e.g., 5/12/20%). Additionally enable an automated batch multiplier that multiplies the committed discount by 1.25x when average batch size > 8 across the billing window.
- Arm B (Commitment only): Same commitment tiers and baseline discounts, but no batch multiplier.
Control: Customers on current per-vector pricing ladder (no commitment).

Primary metrics: net revenue per customer (MRR from commitments + usage), effective per-vector unit price, % of requests batched, average batch size, churn rate at 90 days, and customer-reported satisfaction (NPS survey). Secondary metrics: change in latency percentiles for batched vs non-batched traffic, model quality/VV checks where applicable.

Billing & contract considerations: Draft contract addendum language (billing-credits, rounding rules, chargebacks on refunds, early termination) is in Confluence (CON-emb-pilot-draft). QSA and enterprise sales checklists must reflect: (a) how commitments appear in invoicing, (b) audit trail for consumed credits, (c) reconciliation steps for partial consumption in initial month.

Security / Compliance & QSA work: The pilot must include a short questionnaire addendum to the enterprise security questionnaire clarifying: logging retention for billing events, KMS usage for billing keys, and auditability of batch-aggregation logic. Legal has requested a short tech note explaining that the batch multiplier is a billing construct only and does not change data residency or processing guarantees.

Implementation dependencies: Analytics instrumentation for per-request batch tag, billing pipeline change to apply dynamic multipliers, Console UX surfaces to show committed credits, and Contract templating for Sales. Workstreams have been broken into sub-issues.

Rollout plan: 6-week pilot with up to 50 customers (mix of self-serve and sales-sourced). Week 0: enroll and baseline measurement. Week 1–4: run and monitor metrics daily; stop criteria defined for >5% latency regression on p99 for non-batched critical routes or data integrity errors in billing records. Week 6: readout and decision to (a) iterate pricing tiers, (b) scale to a beta cohort, or (c) cancel.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cheating the batch measurement: add server-side tagging and sample-level verification; require a minimum of 1000 requests for cohort inclusion.
- Negative revenue impact if multiplier too generous: cap the maximum effective discount and run revenue-simulations before each enrollment.
- Legal/Sales complexity: provide templates and a simple one-page FAQ for account teams.

Artifacts: Confluence pilot spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pilot-emb-commitments, initial PR for billing changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/742, analytics dashboard (private): https://app.redwood.ai/dash/emb-commitments-2026
